title: Elizabethtown College debuting new course dedicated to UAPs

content:
ELIZABETHTOWN, Pa. (WHTM) — Elizabethtown College’s School of Graduate and Professional Studies is offering a unique course beginning next year: the study of unidentified anomalous phenomena, or UAP.

The online course, Introduction to UAP Studies, will begin during the spring 2027 semester, in collaboration with The Society for UAP Studies (SUAPS). It will examine UAP “through historical, cultural, psychological and scientific perspectives.”

UAP will be looked at “within an academic setting, emphasizing research, evidence and critical analysis.” Students will learn about all aspects of UAP, along with the more commonly known UFO, from their beginnings to present day.

The college noted that UAP have garnered significant attention over the last few years, particularly from government agencies, scientific institutions and policymakers, including Pentagon reports and hearings with the U.S. House of Representatives.

The course will be co-taught by Dr. Michael D. Silberstein, a professor of philosophy and science, society and technology at E-town College, and Dr. Michael C. Cifone, a 2000 graduate and founding editor of Liminia: The Journal of UAP Studies. Both are co-founders of the SUAPS, with Silberstein serving as secretary and Cifone serving as president.

“UAP studies present an important opportunity for interdisciplinary academic inquiry,” Silberstein said in a press release. “Bringing this subject into a college curriculum creates a structured environment for critical thinking and serious scholarly engagement.”
